CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypogonadism follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Paul Edwards is a 59-year-old HIV-positive male presenting for follow-up of hypogonadism. Patient reports feeling well on current testosterone replacement therapy at 1 mL every 10 days. He reports improved vigor, better sleep, and positive improvements in bloodwork since starting testosterone. Patient notes his cholesterol and triglycerides have improved significantly since starting testosterone on the 28th—triglycerides decreased from 265 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL over 5 months. Red blood cell count has increased and remains stable. PSA is stable at 0.6, down from 0.5 last year. Patient inquired about increasing testosterone dose to 175 mg from current 140 mg but was counseled against dose escalation due to risk of elevated peak levels exceeding 1,500 ng/dL and associated risk of blood viscosity requiring discontinuation. Patient takes finasteride 5 mg at half-pill dose and takes cialis at varying doses—5 mg on days he works out and 2.5 mg otherwise. He reports running out of cialis recently but is otherwise compliant with medications and states he is taking correct steps to improve his life.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports improved sleep and increased vigor on current testosterone regimen.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
HIV positive.
Hypogonadism.
History of elevated triglycerides.

MEDICATIONS
Testosterone 1 mL every 10 days.
Finasteride 2.5 mg daily (half of 5 mg pill).
Cialis 2.5-5 mg daily as needed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works out.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears trim. Heart and lungs auscultated with no concerns noted.

RESULTS
PSA: 0.6 ng/mL (previous 0.5 ng/mL last year).
Testosterone: Previously greater than 1,500 ng/dL.
Cholesterol and triglycerides: Triglycerides decreased from 265 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL. Cholesterol improved.
Red blood cell count: Increased and stable.
Estradiol: Not elevated on previous testing.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
59-year-old HIV-positive male with hypogonadism doing well on current testosterone replacement therapy. Patient responding well clinically and biochemically with improved lipid profile, stable PSA, and improved sense of vigor and sleep. Discussed risks of dose escalation including elevated peak testosterone levels and blood viscosity concerns. Decided to maintain current testosterone dose of 1 mL every 10 days. Patient to continue finasteride 2.5 mg daily and cialis as needed. Estradiol can be rechecked in the fall if desired but not medically necessary at this time. PSA to be checked annually. Paper prescriptions provided for testosterone, finasteride, and cialis. Patient using Walmart pharmacy for all medications.
